get.description:
Liveness and dependency check.

The database is required, so losing it is "down" and returns 503. Redis is a cache,
so losing it is "degraded" and still returns 200 — the app serves from Postgres.

post.description: Create an account and sign in immediately.

Exchange credentials for a token pair.

Wrong password and unknown account return the same 401 with the same message.

Rotate a refresh token.

The presented token is consumed. Replaying a spent one revokes every token in its
family, on the assumption it was stolen.

Revoke the session.

Supplying the refresh token ends the whole family; without it only the current
access token is denylisted.

Begin a password reset.

Always reports success. Telling the caller whether an email is registered would
turn this into an account-enumeration oracle.
Complete a password reset. Ends every existing session for that account.

get.description: The authenticated user's own record.
The authenticated user's own profile, including their email.
Search users by username or display name.

schema.title: Response Search Users Api V1 Users Search Get

get.description:
Another user's public profile.

Returns UserProfile, not OwnProfile — email is absent by construction rather than
by remembering to strip it.

patch.description:
Update a profile by id.

Exists so the ownership check is exercised on an addressable route: being
authenticated does not make someone else's row yours. The service raises 403
unless the id is the caller's own.

post.description: Follow a user. Idempotent — following twice is not an error.

patch.description: Edit your own post. Only fields present in the body change.

delete.description: Delete your own post. Someone else's returns 403.

get.description: A user's posts as the profile grid — pinned first, then newest.
Posts this user is tagged in — the third tab on a profile.
People tagged in a post.

schema.title: Response List Post Tags Api V1 Posts  Post Id  Tags Get

post.description: Tag someone in your own post. Tagging them again moves their marker.

schema.title: Response Add Post Tag Api V1 Posts  Post Id  Tags Post

delete.description:
Remove a tag.

Allowed for the post's author and for the tagged person themselves — being
tagged is something other people do to you, so you must be able to undo it.

get.description: Posts whose caption mentions you, newest first.

post.description: Comment on a post, or reply to a comment by sending `parent_id`.

get.description:
Top-level comments on a post, oldest first.

Replies are not interleaved here — each carries a `replies_count`, and the
thread is fetched from `/comments/{id}/replies`. Mixing them in would let one
busy thread push every other comment off the first page.

post.description:
Reply to a comment.

Threads stay one level deep: replying to a reply attaches to the same top-level
comment rather than nesting further.

get.description: Replies under one comment, oldest first.

delete.description:
Delete a comment.

Allowed for the comment's author, and for the owner of the post it is on so they
can moderate their own content. Anyone else gets 403.

Deleting a top-level comment takes its replies with it.

get.description:
Type-ahead over tags. Prefix match, most used first.

Registered before `/hashtags/{tag}` so the literal path wins — otherwise
"search" would be read as a tag name.

schema.title: Response Search Hashtags Api V1 Hashtags Search Get

get.description: One tag and how many posts carry it.

Posts carrying a tag, newest first, as a grid.

Returns an empty page rather than 404 for a tag nobody has used: a tag landing
page reached by tapping text in a caption should show "nothing here", not an
error.

People and hashtags matching one query.

The client has a single search box, so one call backs it rather than making the
screen fan out to two endpoints and stitch the results together.

A leading "#" narrows the search to tags — that is what typing one means.

post.description:
Get a URL to upload a file directly to storage.

POST the returned `fields` plus the file to `upload_url` as multipart form
data, then call `/media/{asset_id}/confirm`. The storage key is generated
server-side; a caller-supplied path would let one user overwrite another's
object.

Verify the uploaded bytes and make the asset usable.

The file's actual signature is inspected here. A declared content type proves
nothing — anything can claim to be a JPEG.

get.description: A fresh signed URL for an asset. Call again once the previous one expires.

The reels feed, newest first.

Not restricted to accounts you follow — a reels tab limited to your graph would
be empty for a new account, which defeats its purpose.

delete.description: Delete your own reel. Someone else's returns 403.

post.description:
Count a view.

Not deduplicated per user — that needs a row per viewer per reel, a lot of
writes for a number displayed as "820K". Explore ranking tolerates the drift.

schema.title: Response Record View Api V1 Reels  Reel Id  View Post

get.description:
The story tray: one entry per author with unexpired stories.

Grouped by author because that is how the row is drawn — a flat list would push
the grouping onto every client. Your own entry comes first.

schema.title: Response Story Tray Api V1 Stories Get

post.description: Post a story. It stops being visible after 24 hours.

get.description: An author's unexpired stories, oldest first. Expired ones are never returned.

schema.title: Response User Stories Api V1 Users  User Id  Stories Get
Response List Highlights Api V1 Users  User Id  Highlights Get

post.description:
Save stories into a permanent highlight.

Images are copied, not linked — a highlight exists to outlive the stories in
it, so referencing rows that expire would leave it empty.

schema.title: Response Highlight Items Api V1 Highlights  Highlight Id  Items Get

get.description:
The discovery grid: popular reels and recent posts.

Cached under a single key with no viewer component. That is safe *because* the
response carries no per-viewer state — the moment something like is_liked is
added here, this key becomes a cross-user leak and must be scoped like the feed.

Your conversations, most recent first.

Presence for the whole page resolves in one Redis round trip rather than one
call per row.

schema.title: Response List Conversations Api V1 Conversations Get

post.description: Open a direct thread. Returns the existing one if it already exists.

get.description: Total unread across all threads, for the tab badge.

Message history, newest first.

A non-participant gets 404 rather than 403 — a 403 would confirm the thread
exists, which is itself information about other people's conversations.

post.description:
Send a message and push it to every participant's open sockets.

Recipients come from database membership, not from anything the caller supplies.
Advance your read cursor for this thread.

ConversationRow.title: ConversationRow
ConversationRow.description:
The conversation list row, shaped like `MessageData.ts`.

That mock carries `username`, `message`, `time`, `unread`, `online` and `image`
— a thread summary, not a message. This is the same idea with real types:
`unread` is a count rather than a boolean so a badge can show a number, and
`time` is ISO-8601 rather than "now".

CreatePostRequest.title: CreatePostRequest
CreatePostRequest.description:
Either an external image_url or a media_asset_id from a confirmed upload.

media_asset_id is the real path: those bytes have been verified. image_url is
kept for development and for referencing images already hosted elsewhere.

CreateReplyRequest.title: CreateReplyRequest
CreateReplyRequest.description: Body for POST /comments/{id}/replies — the parent comes from the path.

ExploreItem.title: ExploreItem
ExploreItem.description:
Matches `SearchData.tsx` — id, image, views, isVideo.

Note there is nothing viewer-specific here: no is_liked, no is_following. That
is what makes the whole grid cacheable once for everyone rather than per user,
unlike the feed.

OwnProfile.title: OwnProfile
OwnProfile.description: The authenticated user's own profile. Adds their own email, nothing more.

PostAuthor.title: PostAuthor
PostAuthor.description:
Denormalised author, matching what the feed card already renders.

`Posts.ts` reads `username` and `profileImage` straight off each post rather than
joining, so the payload carries them inline.

PostOut.title: PostOut
PostOut.description:
A feed post.

`created_at` is ISO-8601 rather than the mock's pre-formatted "2 hours ago"
(PRD 7.8): relative time depends on when it is read, not when it was sent, and
a cached string goes stale immediately. Counts are numbers, per PRD 7.9.

ProfileLinkOut.title: ProfileLinkOut
ProfileLinkOut.description:
A profile link on the way out.

`url` is a plain str, not HttpUrl, on purpose. The write side above validates
with HttpUrl, so nothing malformed gets stored — but a *response* model that
re-validates would turn one bad legacy row into a 500 on profile read. Validate
on the way in, trust on the way out.

ReelOut.title: ReelOut
ReelOut.description:
Matches what `Reels.ts` renders, with counts as numbers.

The mock stored `likes: "12.5K"`. Abbreviation is a display concern — the API
returns the real number so the client can format it for its locale (PRD 7.9).

SearchResponse.title: SearchResponse
SearchResponse.description:
One call behind the single search box in the client.

The design has one field, not a tabbed people/tags search, so making the client
fan out to two endpoints and stitch the results would push work up for no gain.

StoryTray.title: StoryTray
StoryTray.description:
One row per author, which is how the tray is actually drawn.

A flat list of stories would make the client group them; the mock shows one
circle per person, so the grouping belongs here.

TaggedUser.title: TaggedUser
TaggedUser.description:
Someone tagged in the picture, with where the tag sits on it.

x and y are 0..1 fractions of width and height, not pixels — the client renders
the same image at whatever size the device gives it. Null when the tag was added
without a position.

UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest
UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Every field optional — a PATCH updates only what it sends.

None and "absent" mean different things here: absent leaves a field alone,
while an explicit null clears it. model_fields_set distinguishes them.

UserPrivate.title: UserPrivate
UserPrivate.description: The authenticated user's own record. Adds only their own email.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description:
A profile as seen by anyone.

An explicit allowlist rather than an ORM dump. email, password_hash,
failed_login_count and locked_until are absent by construction, so adding a
column later cannot silently expose it.

UserSummary.title: UserSummary
UserSummary.description:
Compact shape for lists — followers, following, search results.

No email: this is other people's data.
